notes:
- Company background: Mid-market SaaS (product search for e-commerce clients). Heavy emphasis on product UX; search relevance is core to conversion. Currently operate Elasticsearch + simple learned reranker (light BERT) hosted in AWS Lambda for scoring.
- Why Redwood: liked streaming + hosted API for fast iteration; sees clear path to Dedicated for predictable cost at scale and VPC for client data residency.
- POC goals: evaluate Redwood rerank endpoint vs current pipeline. Key success metrics: +10-15% NDCG@10 uplift, stable p95 latency <50ms, 40-60% reduction in per-query cost vs current Lambda FLOPs when using Dedicated with batching/kv caching.
- Technical asks: support for passing candidate doc ids + context, offline scoring API to compute scores across full corpus (10-20M docs) overnight, API to export re-ranker scores for downstream analytics, ability to run holdout A/B with canary traffic routing.
- Security/compliance: require SSO (SAML), SOC2 attestation, audit logs retention 1 year, KMS integration for model keys, data residency in us-east-1 for enterprise clients.
- Quote from head of product: "We need reranks to be fast and explainable — give us scores we can tie to features and lookup. If latency is good and cost predictable we'll move to Dedicated."
- POC constraints: internal SSO migration slated for May — affects timeline. Legal wants changes to SLA around data deletion and incident notifications.
- Pricing posture: cost-sensitive but pragmatic — will commit to Dedicated if POC shows >=30% unit-cost improvement and parity on relevance.
- Next immediate actions: send Dedicated pricing slide + POC SOW, grant S3 eval bucket to Redwood, schedule 60m POC kickoff with infra + security (proposed 2026-02-22).
